title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - A-36
notes:
West's heart lead drives out South's ♥A. There are only 6 top tricks, 2 spades, the ♥A, the ♦A, and 2 clubs. South must hope for diamonds to provide the 3 additional tricks that are required. South should plan to finesse West for the ♦K. If West has 2 or 3 diamonds the contract will be made easily.

South can guard against West holding a singleton ♦K by leading a low diamond (as opposed to the ♦Q or ♦J) on the first round of the suit. When West follows with the ♦K, South has no trouble taking 4 diamond tricks.

Due to the presence of the ♦7 in dummy, South has a stronger play available. South should start with the ♦Q or ♦J. This play will be immediately fatal if West began with a singleton ♦K. It is necessary, however, to start diamonds this way in the more likely event the East has a singleton ♦9 or ♦8.

If West covers with the ♦K, South wins the ♦A as East follows with a high spot card. South can cross back to his remaining diamond honor and finesse against West's high diamond spot card.

If West does not cover on the first round of diamonds, South must continue with his other diamond honor. If West ducks again, South can finesse the ♦10 on the third round. If West covers on the second round, South can win the ♦A, cross back to his hand and finesse against West's high spot card in diamonds.

On the previous deal, a singleton ♦K with West was the only 4-1 break that could be picked up. As the diamond spots in dummy are stronger on this deal, South must choose between picking up a singleton ♦K with West or picking up a singleton ♦9 or ♦8 with East. As there are 2 combinations that favor starting with a diamond honor (versus 1 combination for starting with a low diamond), it is correct to play the ♦Q or ♦J on the first round.
